title: Mollification of a Lipschitz function: smooth, same Lipschitz constant, uniform convergence, a.e. convergence of derivatives
statement: Let k ∈ ℕ, L ∈ ℝ≥0 and f : ℝᵏ → ℝ L-Lipschitz (ℝᵏ = Euclid k with Lebesgue measure). Then there are functions f_n : ℝᵏ → ℝ (n ∈ ℕ) such that every f_n is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)), every f_n is L-Lipschitz, f_n → f uniformly on ℝᵏ, and Df_n(x) → Df(x) in operator norm for Lebesgue-a.e. x ∈ ℝᵏ, where D = fderiv ℝ (Df(x) = 0 where f is not differentiable).
lean_statement: ∀ (k : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (f : Euclid k → ℝ), LipschitzWith L f → ∃ fs : ℕ → Euclid k → ℝ, (∀ n, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (fs n)) ∧ (∀ n, LipschitzWith L (fs n)) ∧ TendstoUniformly fs f atTop ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂(volume : Measure (Euclid k)), Tendsto (fun n => fderiv ℝ (fs n) x) atTop (𝓝 (fderiv ℝ f x))
